body.x: In Alzheimer's programs, up to 80% of candidates are excluded through invasive workups, and procedures such as lumbar puncture, PET/CT and biopsy are costly.

iLOF - Intelligent Lab on Fiber, Unipessoal Lda, a health-tech company led by CEO Luís Valente, exhibited Optomics® at the 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026), held from Oct. 13 to 16 at COEX in Seoul. iLOF serves healthcare and biopharma, supporting early disease detection, patient stratification and drug development. Optomics® is a patented precision-diagnostics platform that combines photonics and AI. iLOF is seeking health systems for lung cancer risk triage, pharmaceutical companies for patient pre-selection and enrichment in clinical trials, and collaborators for prospective validation cohorts.

Optomics® generates a multi-dimensional digital biological fingerprint from microliters of serum or plasma. A compact benchtop instrument uses label-free optical spectroscopy to capture thousands of spectral data points that reflect the concentration, composition and structure of native biomolecules. The only preparation needed is centrifugation, with no chemical labels or reagents. According to the company, the platform captures the optical fingerprint of a blood sample in under 30 seconds. iLOF says that in clinical trial screening it can cut screening costs by up to 40% and screening time by 70%.

The company's key differentiator is that a single blood draw can support screening across multiple diseases. Because the hardware captures a complete molecular profile, new diagnostics are deployed through software updates, so the same instrument can be retrained for oncology and neurodegeneration without hardware changes or new capital expenditure. ML models trained on a healthy reference cohort of more than 500 people across four sites filter out age, gender and lifestyle confounders.

In lung cancer (n=133), the platform achieved an AUROC of 0.99 in cross-validated testing and 95% sensitivity on an independent, blinded external cohort. In late-stage ovarian cancer (n=256), it achieved an AUROC of 0.93. Specificity of 91% to 96% was confirmed against a 1,449-sample panel spanning more than 10 other conditions. iLOF positions Optomics® as an intelligent pre-filter ahead of invasive or costly procedures such as lumbar puncture, PET/CT and biopsy.

The technology is also used in drug development. iLOF says it has proven effective in measuring parameters of drugs in liquid samples, such as payload, concentration and particle size, which makes quality control more efficient and removes the need for costly reagents that destroy samples or entire batches. It is running pilot studies with the Portuguese pharmaceutical company Bluepharma, supported by paid pilots with RNA T&T (Canada) and Karolinska Institutet (Sweden).

iLOF has raised about EUR 20 million. Equity investors include the venture funds Microsoft M12, Hamamatsu Ventures and re.Mind Capital, and non-dilutive funding has come from European institutions and programs including the European Innovation Council, national government-supported schemes, Eurostars and Innomatch.

According to iLOF, it signed a USD 1.5 million contract with the Global Alzheimer's Platform (GAP) to deploy Optomics® in Biohermes-002, described as the largest Alzheimer's disease study in the world. The multi-center study spans more than 30 hospitals in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom and is supported by pharmaceutical companies including Roche, Merck and AbbVie. iLOF also has a strategic partnership with Hamamatsu Photonics of Japan, and in Asia it is a partner of Johnson & Johnson after winning an award that gives it access to the company's JLABS facilities across the region.

At MWC Barcelona in 2021, iLOF received the GSMA 4YFN Impact Award and was a finalist on the Discovery Stage. In 2024, it was named Outstanding Graduate and placed second at the Luminate Finals in New York. At the World Economic Forum in Davos in 2025, it won the Founders Games competition after evaluation by more than 400 venture capital investors. Sifted has featured iLOF among photonics startups to follow, and the European Investment Fund has published its growth model as an official case study.

iLOF currently exports to the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada. Its target markets are those three countries plus Japan, South Korea, Singapore and EU countries including Spain, Germany, France, the Netherlands and Italy. It is looking for clinical and research institutions to test Optomics® in their clinical workflows and to provide well-characterized samples of Alzheimer's disease, lung cancer and ovarian cancer, as well as specialized clinical equipment manufacturers that can turn its prototype device into a final product for clinical laboratories and primary or secondary care institutions.

Its export efforts now center on the United States, which it cites for access to the largest clinical research and pharmaceutical market, access to a top-tier venture capital firm that could lead a Series A round, and proximity to major innovation hubs. To get there, iLOF plans to establish a CLIA lab to analyze American cohorts and to incorporate in the United States. In the EU, it plans prospective lung cancer studies in Germany, Spain and France, in addition to a clinical prospective study already approved in Portugal that is scheduled to begin in early 2027. It is also exploring the Asia-Pacific region through Hamamatsu's established reach, and aims to bring PET scan results into its platform to improve its AI models.

The 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026) ran from Oct. 13 (Tuesday) to 16 (Friday) in Halls A and B at COEX in Seoul. The Korea Electronics Association (KEA) organized the show, and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources hosted it. The KES website lists 500 exhibitors and 1,100 booths. Its themes included electronic parts and materials such as sensors, connectors, printed circuit boards (PCBs) and power supplies; AI transformation (AX) fields such as generative AI, on-device AI, AI chips and smart home and wearable devices; mobility; robotics; digital health; ESG; and Web 3.0 and XR. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event featured X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony took place on Oct. 13.
